mechanism_narrative: A lower federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) indicates accommodative monetary policy, reducing discount rates for equity valuations and generating positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 55% of periods with FEDFUNDS below 4.0% (t-test p-value > 0.05 vs. zero).

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate exceeds 4.5%, it signals a restrictive monetary policy that increases equity discount rates, causing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of periods with FEDFUNDS > 4.5% (t-test p-value > 0.05 vs. zero).

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in unemployment rate (UNRATE) and decline in payrolls (PAYEMS) indicates deteriorating labor market conditions, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: The joint signal of rising UNRATE and falling PAYEMS fails to predict negative returns in more than 55% of cases (Rank IC < 0.03 over 3-year rolling window).

mechanism_narrative: In high GDP growth regimes (GDPC1 > 2.5% annualized), rising housing starts (HOUST) signal robust consumer demand, driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: HOUST rises but SPX 60-day returns are negative in more than 55% of high GDP growth periods (t-test p-value > 0.05 vs. zero).

mechanism_narrative: A higher unemployment rate (UNRATE) reflects weak labor market conditions, reducing consumer spending and corporate earnings, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of periods with UNRATE above 4.0% (t-test p-value > 0.05 vs. zero).

mechanism_narrative: A decline in industrial production (INDPRO) below 100 indicates weakening manufacturing activity, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of periods with INDPRO < 100 (t-test p-value > 0.05 vs. zero).

mechanism_narrative: A joint increase in housing starts (HOUST) and retail sales (RSAFS) signals strong consumer demand, generating positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The combined signal of rising HOUST and RSAFS fails to predict positive returns in more than 55% of cases (Rank IC < 0.03 over 3-year rolling window).

mechanism_narrative: In high inflation regimes (CPIAUCSL > 5% annualized), a rising federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) signals aggressive monetary tightening, causing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of periods with CPIAUCSL > 5% and rising FEDFUNDS (t-test p-value > 0.05 vs. zero).
